title: Outsourcing payroll: a lopsided range, and a hedge that wins on average
story: Running payroll in-house costs a known EUR 104k over three years. The vendor quotes EUR 100k, and that is the likely cost, but implementations overrun: the range runs from 95k to 220k. A hybrid outsources processing but keeps one payroll lead in-house: half of each cost, less 1.5k of vendor change fees it avoids. On the likely values outsourcing leads by 500; it is cheapest in 54% of worlds; yet on average the hybrid is cheapest (103.1k vs 104k in-house vs 105.1k outsourced). The hybrid leads only in narrow bands of each number. A non-default random seed (7) is used.
source: Marritt, 'Should you replace Sam?': point estimates and their spread ('Average it away and you never see it'), and the README's close-call rule (average and likely values disagree)
